question.text: Mr. Arun Mehra applies for Accredited Investor status. His profile: annual income INR 1.5 crore, net worth INR 6 crore (of which INR 3 crore is financial assets and INR 3 crore is the value of his primary residence). Is he eligible under the Individual AI framework?

answer.text: Yes - annual income of INR 1.5 crore exceeds the INR 1 crore threshold
No - under the combined test, his qualifying net worth is INR 3 crore (excluding primary residence), which is below the INR 5 crore minimum required at the INR 1 crore income level
Yes - total net worth of INR 6 crore alone satisfies the INR 5 crore combined test
No - individual AI threshold is a flat INR 10 crore net worth

explanation.text: The Logic: Individual AI thresholds include a combined test requiring annual income of at least INR 1 crore together with net worth of at least INR 5 crore (with a financial-asset sub-test). Primary residence is excluded from the net-worth calculation. Here, Mr. Mehra's qualifying net worth = 6 crore - 3 crore (primary residence) = INR 3 crore, which is below the INR 5 crore floor under the combined test. His income alone does not satisfy the standalone income-only threshold. The Trap: Option A misapplies the standalone income test. Option C forgets the primary-residence exclusion from net-worth, a classic AI framework trap. Option D states a flat INR 10 crore net-worth figure that is not the rule. Note: The workbook supports the individual AI thresholds, the exclusion of primary residence from the net-worth calculation, and continuation of AI status through the scheme life once onboarded as an AI.
